description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5) while shipping #478.

MEASURED over the cpan-t census population (289 files, one pl2cl process each,
the population the Test::/Test2:: name list used to serve):

  with the name skip (HEAD before s446k)   65.5 s   83 drops
  without it (s446k)                      281.3 s   11 drops

The 4.3x is one mechanism: `use Test2::API qw/intercept/` makes
_extract_module_prototypes walk 27 modules / 242 KB of perl through PPI, and
`state $cache` inside that sub dies with the process.  So the same 242 KB is
re-parsed 289 times.

THE RULED FALLBACK (a BUDGET on the recursive walk, s439) WAS IMPLEMENTED,
MEASURED AND REJECTED -- do not re-attempt it without reading this:

  budget (bytes, nested walks only)   289 files    40 files
  none                                281.3 s      37.9 s
  128 KB                                 --        51.6 s   <- SLOWER than none
   32 KB                               212.0 s      27.3 s
    0 (own includes only)              162.4 s      23.8 s

The curve is not monotone because a TRUNCATED walk cannot go in the
process-wide memo: caching it would make file 2's emission depend on how much
budget file 1 had left (`pl2cl --server` transpiles many files from one
process), so a cut forces re-walks, and the more you walk before cutting the
more you re-walk.  Only the extreme (never recurse) was faster, and that one
breaks a genuine re-export chain -- measured: `use Encode` in perl-tests/tr.t
reaches Encode::Alias / Encode::MIME::Name / Storable at depth 2, and at 32 KB
tr.t was the ONE perl-tests file that took a budget cut.

THE FIX SHAPE: memoize the FACTS ACROSS PROCESSES.  The walk is pure (module
path + content -> prototypes + export_names), the serialisation already exists
and was validated over 95 modules in s412 (`PCL_PROTO_ORACLE`'s JSON dump: the
prototype records and the export names, which is EXACTLY what
_merge_module_prototypes consumes), and PCL already has a keyed on-disk cache
family under ~/.pcl-cache.  Sketch: key = module absolute path + mtime + size +
`*pcl-cache-generation*` (a collect_prototypes change is an emission change);
atomic write (temp + rename, the s339/s340 rule -- `prove -j8` and the census
run many processes at once); rebuild an env with add_prototype + export_names.
Expected: the census population back to ~70 s WITH the correct parse, and a
real user transpiling a test suite pays the walk once instead of per file.

BAR: corpus-diff IDENTICAL (the cache must not change emission, only its
cost); the same 289-file timing re-run; a cold/warm A/B; a deliberately
corrupted cache entry must be detected, not used.  MEASURE the hit rate: if
most modules are read once per RUN anyway the win is smaller than it looks.


RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): APPROVED -- memoize the walk-s FACTS on disk, PER MODULE.  Design pins: (1) cache family ~/.pcl-cache/proto/, ONE ENTRY PER MODULE, so the recursive walk consults the cache before recursing (a hit prunes the branch; one module-s change invalidates one entry); (2) key = module absolute path + mtime + size + *pcl-cache-generation* (a collect-prototypes change is an emission change -- the bump discipline already exists), hashed into the filename AND repeated inside the JSON so a mismatch on read = ignored + rebuilt (the corrupted-entry bar); (3) value = the PCL_PROTO_ORACLE record shape (prototype records + export_names, validated over 95 modules s412; the dump code at Pl/Parser.pm:9026-9131 is the serializer to reuse); (4) atomic write temp+rename (s339/s340 -- prove -j8 and the census run many processes); (5) the in-process state memo stays as L1.  Bar as listed: corpus-diff IDENTICAL (cost only, never emission), the 289-file timing re-run, cold/warm A/B, corrupted-entry detection, hit rate measured.  The budget stays REJECTED (this task-s own table).  Opus builds, round 8 or next.

SHIPPED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U, 2026-08-29) — `Pl/ProtoCache.pm`.

Built to the ruled design: one entry per MODULE under `~/.pcl-cache/proto/`,
consulted in `_extract_module_prototypes` AFTER the cycle check and path
resolution and BEFORE the walk, so a hit prunes the whole branch; key = the
module's absolute path + mtime + size + `*pcl-cache-generation*`, hashed into
the filename AND repeated inside the JSON (mismatch = ignored + rebuilt);
value = the `PCL_PROTO_ORACLE` record shape (prototypes + export_names, plus
`pkg_prototypes` and the walk's end `current_package`, which `get_prototype`
consults); atomic temp+rename; the `state` memo kept as L1.

MEASURED, 289 cpan-t files, one `pl2cl` process each, serial, this machine:

    no cache (the baseline)          226.6 s wall / 212.4 s child CPU
    interleaved A/B, same run        209.9 s no-cache vs 68.4 s cached
                                     287 files byte-SAME, 0 DIFF, 2 empty both sides
    COLD population pass              78.0 s   hit 605 / miss 104 (85.3 %), 98 stores
    WARM                              62.3 s   hit 608 / miss 6  (99.0 %),  0 stores
    WARM again                        62.3 s   identical — stable

A cold PASS is already fast because file 1 warms the other 288; the 4.3x the
task predicted is what a single file sees (0.70 s -> 0.13 s on `use Test2::API`).

EMISSION IDENTICAL — the first and non-negotiable leg, four ways:
  * `tools/corpus-diff.pl`: identical across 111 files + 6 shapes, silent
    drops 5, unchanged;
  * `tools/emission-ab.pl --ref e2a7567`: 23 lib shims SAME/0 DIFF, and
    500 files (cpan `.pm` + cpan-t + perl-tests + shapes) SAME / 0 DIFF /
    0 RCDIFF;
  * in-tree A/B (`PCL_NO_PROTO_CACHE=1` vs warm): 289 cpan-t + 30 perl-tests,
    0 DIFF;
  * `pl2cl --server`: the same fragment transpiled in forward order, reverse
    order and alone gives the same bytes, cache on and cache off (the L1+L2
    cross-contamination check).  `parse_source` resets the walk-frame stack
    per SOURCE so a died transpile cannot leave a half-unwound stack.

THREE STRENGTHENINGS of the pinned key, each a silent wrong without it (the
argument is in the module's POD, and each has a guard row):
  1. a COMPILER stamp — the `Pl/` dir's absolute path plus every `Pl/**.pm`'s
     mtime+size.  The facts are a function of the code that derived them, and
     this is also what keeps two worktrees that share a generation string from
     reading each other's entries (PCLSbcl's rule for a saved core).
  2. the DEPENDENCY list the walk resolved (name, resolved path, mtime, size),
     re-resolved AND re-stat'ed on every hit.  The facts an entry holds are
     dependency-inclusive, so "a dependency changed" and "a dependency now
     resolves elsewhere" (a dist's `t/lib`) both have to invalidate.
  3. a walk whose answer depends on WHERE THE PROCESS STARTED is never stored:
     cycle-truncated (taint marks every frame on the stack and propagates
     through the L1 memo) or one that changed `@INC` under itself (`use lib`
     inside a module, detected by comparing the inc_paths list across the
     walk).  MEASURED over the whole population: taint fires for exactly
     `Encode` and `Encode::Alias`, which use each other, in 3 of 289 files —
     and those 6 lookups are precisely the warm pass's 6 misses.

Guard `Pl/t/proto-cache-01.t`, 12 rows, ~1 s, no SBCL: cold/warm byte
identity, no second write, cache-off identity, a CORRUPTED entry ignored and
rebuilt, a key mismatch ignored, a touched module and a touched DEPENDENCY
both invalidating (the dependency row makes a REAL emission change, so it
would fail if the entry survived).

Switches: `PCL_NO_PROTO_CACHE=1` off, `PCL_PROTO_STATS=1` hit/miss/stale/
store/taint on exit, `=2` also names the modules, `pcl --clear-cache` removes
the entries and reports the count.  `pl2cl`'s `cache_generation` now delegates
to `Pl::ProtoCache::generation` — ONE reader of `*pcl-cache-generation*`.

NO generation bump: the change is emission-identical by construction, and the
cache key already carries the generation, so a bump would only invalidate the
runtime's module caches for nothing.

RESIDUE FILED: #681 (`_extract_file_prototypes` — the `require './test.pl'`
walk — is still per-process; measure before doing), #682 (no pruning).
subject: The module prototype pre-scan is memoized PER PROCESS, so every pl2cl pays the whole transitive PPI parse again -- 4.3x on any file that reaches the Test2 stack (the cost #478's name list was hiding)
